Check youth pitch counts against Pitch Smart guidelines

Source: R/check_pitch_counts.R
check_pitch_counts.Rd

Apply the MLB/USA Baseball Pitch Smart daily maximums and required rest days to a log of pitching appearances. Each pitcher's days are checked in date order, so a pitcher who returns before the required rest is flagged along with any day over the age group's maximum.

Usage

check_pitch_counts(appearances, rules = daimondstats::pitch_smart_rules)

Arguments

appearances

A data frame with one row per pitching appearance and columns pitcher (nonempty character), age (whole number from 7 to 18 on the game date), date (a Date or "YYYY-MM-DD" text), and pitches (nonnegative whole number). Extra columns are ignored.

rules

A rules table with the columns of pitch_smart_rules. Leagues with stricter limits can pass an edited copy.

Value

One row per pitcher and date, ordered by pitcher and date, with pitcher, date, age, pitches, appearances (rows combined that day), daily_max, rest_days, next_eligible (first date the pitcher may pitch again), over_max, short_rest, and status, which is "ok", "over daily max", "short rest", or both joined by "; ".

Details

The daily maximum applies to a calendar day, so two appearances on the same date (for example, a doubleheader) are added together before checking. Required rest is counted in calendar days: two days of rest after pitching on Saturday means the pitcher is next eligible on Tuesday. A day over the maximum still receives the largest rest band.

Pitch counts come from the scorecard's pitcher box. A missed or misread count changes the result, so review the counts first. The check only covers the games in appearances; pitching for another team or league is invisible to it. Ages 19 to 22 are not supported because the published rest table does not cover their full daily maximum.

References

Major League Baseball and USA Baseball. n.d. "Pitching Guidelines." Pitch Smart. Accessed November 26, 2026. https://www.mlb.com/pitch-smart/pitching-guidelines.

See also

pitch_smart_rules

Examples

log <- data.frame(
  pitcher = c("Ava", "Ava", "Ben", "Ben"),
  age = c(11, 11, 12, 12),
  date = c("2026-05-02", "2026-05-04", "2026-05-02", "2026-05-03"),
  pitches = c(60, 30, 90, 10)
)
check_pitch_counts(log)
#>   pitcher       date age pitches appearances daily_max rest_days next_eligible
#> 1     Ava 2026-05-02  11      60           1        85         3    2026-05-06
#> 2     Ava 2026-05-04  11      30           1        85         1    2026-05-06
#> 3     Ben 2026-05-02  12      90           1        85         4    2026-05-07
#> 4     Ben 2026-05-03  12      10           1        85         0    2026-05-04
#>   over_max short_rest         status
#> 1    FALSE      FALSE             ok
#> 2    FALSE       TRUE     short rest
#> 3     TRUE      FALSE over daily max
#> 4    FALSE       TRUE     short rest
